highlights.title: Google says its Gemini AI model hacked three other companies
highlights.summary: Disclosure comes after OpenAI and Anthropic hacks amid fears that tech firms unable to control powerful AI models. In a first for Google, the company confirmed that its AI model, Gemini, breached the security of three other companies in May.
body: Irregular, an Israel-based startup that scrutinizes the security of advanced AI systems, was also at the center of some of the recent OpenAI and Anthropic hacks of third-party entities, including OpenAI’s breach of AI software company, Hugging Face.

The circumstances that enabled the models to hack other companies in some of these cases are similar: Irregular was testing the models in a closed testing environment with fake companies. The testing environment was not supposed to be internet enabled, but internet access was made available unintentionally, according to the Wall Street Journal. Once connected to the internet, the models unexpectedly hacked into real firms.

Irregular disclosed the hacks to Google at the end of July after discovering OpenAI hacked into Hugging Face. Google confirmed to the Guardian that the hacks occurred, but that the company did not feel it required public disclosure because the models did not damage the companies. The Wall Street Journal first reported on the breaches and revealed for the first time that they occurred.
points: Disclosure comes after OpenAI and Anthropic hacks amid fears that tech firms unable to control powerful AI models.
In a first for Google, the company confirmed that its AI model, Gemini, breached the security of three other companies in May.

highlights.title: Here’s How an AI Slowdown Could Actually Be Enforced
highlights.summary: Even if big AI companies agree to a pause, ensuring that nobody tries to sneak ahead could prove tricky.
body: Many AI researchers seem to firmly believe that the technology they are developing could someday prove very dangerous. What’s less clear—even among AI’s technical elite —is precisely how to keep these mercurial algorithms in check.

In recent years researchers have thrown around all sorts of ideas for preventing AI from turning nasty. They include less controversial plans such as tighter government regulations, new ways of measuring progress, and probing the inner workings of models, as well as more outlandish proposals like placing tracking devices inside GPUs, and even ceremonially destroying large numbers of AI chips.
With political and public pressure now growing for a more measured approach to building AI, however, the answer to keeping AI safe is still unclear.

“We need to start treating this as a research problem,” says Raymond Douglas, an AI researcher at the University of Toronto and coauthor of a new report titled Pacing the Frontier, A Research Agenda, which warns that slowing down AI development remains an unsolved puzzle. “We don't really understand what our options even are or what they will do.”

highlights.summary: "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.
body: Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.
And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

body: The Resident Evil movie reboot has finally arrived, coming from one of the biggest names in horror these days, filmmaker Zach Cregger, who previously wowed fans with his films Barbarian and Weapons. And he certainly seems to be off to a good start with Resident Evil -- we gave it an 8 out of 10 here at IGN, it's in the 90s on both the Rotten Tomatoes critics and audience scores, and it's on track to be a winner at the box office as well.

IGN's own Tom Jorgensen recently sat down with Cregger and the film's star Austin Abrams -- who plays Bryan, a medical courier with some serious bad luck -- to discuss the divided fan response to the film before it came out, how Cregger and his team went about evoking a true "video game feel" with the reboot, how Abrams almost got killed by a 150-pound bag of blood during production (!), and much more.
You can watch the discussion at the video above, or read it all right here...
Tom Jorgensen for IGN: There is a little bit of a conversation going on about this movie about to what degree it's staying faithful to the games.

body: Chris Brown delivered divergent statements to Texas state Rep. Venton Jones and U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett, the two Texas Democrats who honored him and Usher at the Arlington stop on their co-headlining tour, as controversy swirls around the polarizing pop star’s official recognition by the two lawmakers.
“We are experiencing Black joy to the highest level,” Crockett said at the concert. “And I wanted to make sure we document that at the congressional level. So let’s give it up again for Chris Brown.”

Crockett has not made a public statement this week regarding the event at AT&T Stadium. But speculation has run wild as to why a lawmaker known for taking President Trump to task and equating him to an abusive partner while advocating for abortion access and diversity, equity and inclusion would go out of her way to sing the praises of someone so associated with violence against women. A New York magazine article on Friday floated several potential explanations for her reasoning, from drumming up voter support before the midterms to her eye for a post-politics career as a celebrity.

highlights.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
highlights.summary: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
body: India has extended its anti-spam regime to require caller-ID and call-management apps to share users’ spam reports with telecom operators, prompting spam-blocking app maker Truecaller to call the ruling anti-competitive.

On Friday, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), the country’s telecom regulator, amended rules governing commercial communications, making it mandatory for call-ID and call-management apps that let users flag calls as spam or junk to send those reports to a blockchain-based platform maintained by telecom operators. The platform tracks commercial communications and enforces anti-spam rules.

The change, TRAI said, is intended to broaden the pool of spam reports available for action against spammers, effectively connecting reports collected by apps with the telecom industry’s enforcement infrastructure.

However, Truecaller told TechCrunch that it sees this requirement as a “one-way exchange” that is “anti-competitive,” arguing that it transfers commercially valuable data from call-management apps like itself to telecom operators.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.
Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.

highlights.title: Cottage Cheese Lasagna
highlights.summary: Love cottage cheese? You’ll love this lasagna. Hate cottage cheese? You’ll still love this lasagna.
body: Cottage cheese lasagna skeptics, hear us out. Unlike ricotta, which can turn chalky, small-curd, whole-milk cottage cheese stays moist through the long bake. And when mixed with nutty Parmesan, melty Fontina, eggs, and garlic, it makes an exceptionally creamy lasagna filling.
This may not be nonna’s classic (we’ve got BA’s Best Lasagna for that), but it’s deeply savory, exceptionally cheesy, and considerably easier to assemble.
Whole-milk cottage cheese is nonnegotiable. Lighter versions can make the lasagna watery and less flavorful. We prefer small-curd for texture, but large-curd works just fine if that’s what you have.

Regular dried lasagna noodles go directly into the baking dish—no boiling or soaking required. The relatively loose tomato sauce provides enough moisture to cook the noodles until al dente as the lasagna bakes.

highlights.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
highlights.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger ordered the state government to take steps that could empower local communities to have a larger say in data center development and slow down approvals in a state that is already home to the data center capital of the world.
body: Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed an executive order addressing data centers and AI risks.

Executive Order 22 bans executive branch officials from signing nondisclosure agreements for data center projects, requires expedited noise regulations, and requires a review of backup-generation operations used by data centers, among other requirements. The order also establishes an AI task force responsible for evaluating how the state government can address risks to Virginians like workforce displacement and data privacy issues, and determining how existing law can be applied to AI harms.

The order represents the latest signal that states are taking data center and AI policy into their own hands as Congress and President Donald Trump have been slow or resistant to sweeping changes. Also on Friday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order convening experts to tackle AI safety issues, and earlier, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott have both taken executive action to rein in rapid data center development.

body: Steven Kolb is stepping down from his role as CEO of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA), the organization announced on Friday night.

“Steven Kolb has been a dedicated leader and tireless champion of American fashion throughout his more than two decades at the CFDA, including 15 years as CEO,” the CFDA Board said in a statement. “We respect Steven’s decision to step down and are grateful for his many years of leadership and service to the CFDA and our industry. He leaves the organization well positioned, with a clear mission and dedicated team, to carry out the important work ahead as we look to the future of American fashion.”

“After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organization to begin a new chapter.”

highlights.title: A startup that builds other startups raised $100M and is all-in on physical AI
highlights.summary: UP.Labs, now doing business under the name Vantora, is building startups for industrial corporations.
body: Four years ago, a startup lab launched that wasn’t quite an incubator, accelerator program, or venture firm. UP.Labs, as it was called then, built startups designed to solve problems for corporate customers such as Alaska Airlines and Porsche, as well as for the outside world.

The firm still has the same mission — albeit with a critical addition to its approach, a new name, and a $100 million investment from Silversmith Capital Partners. Vantora, as the firm is now called, continues to work with its corporate customers, including some new ones in industrial manufacturing that it declined to name, and in the oil and gas sector.
But now it’s more focused on building startups solely for its corporate customers and not for the broader market.

Founder and CEO John Kuolt told TechCrunch that Vantora is moving toward a “proprietary M&A pipeline.” This means Vantora will still build startups for its corporate partners, which invest in the ventures and serve as their first customers. But those corporate partners now have the option to fold the startups into their core businesses — and essentially keep them to themselves.

highlights.summary: Someone playing Refractive Entertainment's recently released action-RPG Luminary for less than an hour accused the team of using AI for the game's only voiced character. The player said the voice "killed it" for them. There was just one problem: It wasn't AI.
body: Refractive Entertainment launched Luminary into Steam Early Access on August 11. It's a resource-gathering action-adventure sandbox with an art style that's giving Fable meets Immortals Fenyx Rising. It's cute-looking and well-received, with a "Mostly Positive" rating out of almost 350 Steam reviews. But for an indie developer who says his game's success lives and dies by its Steam review score, one particular negative review caught the creative director's attention.

On September 10, user NyteKnyte posted a short Steam review after only 0.4 hours with the game to say that Luminary looked good but "the awful AI-generated voice killed it" for them. "Feels off, like an AI game," NyteKnyte said in their review. "Hopefully its temporary and gets better, but [the AI voice] killed it for me."
Not long after this review hit the game's Steam page, Refractive Entertainment responded, saying that the “awful AI-generated voice” that NyteKnyte decried was actually the creative director's wife.

highlights.title: Spot the conversation hogger – and do something about it | Letter
highlights.summary: Penelope Mavor suggests that listening is not a passive act, so you could interrupt the flow. These conversational hoggers … don’t they know we were born with two ears and one mouth for a reason?
body: It is an interesting reflection to see which of the five hoggers more frequently turn up in our own lives. As a people pleaser and introvert, I have a track record of meeting many monologuists. I pretend to listen, but secretly resent them and their audacity. I just want them to ask about me.

I have learned that although interruption can feel violent, sometimes it is a courageous act. When the speaker has just lost connection with the audience and themselves, we have to bring them back. That is what I loved most about the article – it reminded us that we do have options. We can start noticing how we turn up. How am I listening and speaking? What is my responsibility here?
A great listener can help to transform the conversation – listening is not a passive act. And in talking, am I actually being interesting? Am I talking as if being listened to?

highlights.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
highlights.summary: Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times ' case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies' own documentation warned that it was starting a "doom loop" that would damage the web, characterized its scraping of data to train its models as the "largest theft of labor…
body: The companies knew they were driving us toward Google Zero, and did it anyway.

Many of the most eye-catching quotes from the document come from Microsoft’s Director of Applied Science, Brent Hecht. Though, the company has tried to distance itself from Hecht’s assertions. Microsoft spokesperson Alex Haurek told The Verge that “These comments reflect one employee’s individual perspective, are not a legal analysis, and do not represent the company’s views.”

In a separate court filing, Jordan Usdan, GM for Data Strategy and Ops at Microsoft AI, characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial. He said that Hecht “holds divergent, academic, and forward-looking views about how data ecosystems for AI should operate and is employed at Microsoft to bring asymmetrical, futuristic, and academic points of view … nor is he someone who speaks for Microsoft specifically as to his theoretical views on AI’s potential effect on content creators.”
But whether or not Microsoft wants to own these comments, it’s clear that this came true. Google Zero is real! AI is eating the web!

highlights.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
highlights.summary: AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Anthropic researchers have also been warning that AI might kill us all.
body: Anthropic has a wet biology lab in the Bay Area where it can use its AI models to run physical experiments, it has confirmed to TechCrunch.

“We believe that to do biology, the final test is still, and will be for a while, in real lab work,” Anthropic’s head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams, told Reuters. “We absolutely are doing that today.” He added that the lab operates like most biotech labs: Anthropic conducts some research there while also working with external partners.
This news probably shouldn’t be shocking. Anthropic bought Coefficient Bio, a stealth AI biotech, in April.
While Anthropic declined to give specifics on what the wet lab is working on, it did say the main focus was fundamental biology, not drug discovery.

highlights.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will require around 200GB of storage when it launches next year, director Naoki Hamaguchi has warned. The Square Enix developer talked about the install requirements for the remake trilogy's long-awaited conclusion during an interview with VGC.
body: "Things are still getting worked out, but it’s probably going to be around 200GB of game," Hamaguchi said when asked about additional downloads for physical versions of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. "I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent.

"One thing I want to say is, even though the game will not be on the full disc, in the position we’re in, because discs may be dying out, or maybe staying, with Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, we definitely wanted to deliver some kind of physical product. That was really important to us. Trust me!"

Managing installed games sometimes feels like packing a suitcase for a trip. Stuffing your chosen storage space with the essentials means having to choose what comes with you and what stays home, so when a big game comes along and asks to fill storage space with shiny new graphics and giant worlds to explore, hard decisions have to be made if you don't want to shell out the cash for more room. Individual install sizes often vary between platforms, but it's still something players have tried to learn to deal with as games grow increasingly complex.

highlights.title: Marks and Spencer’s first LFW catwalk gamble pays off with compelling looks at affordable prices
highlights.summary: Retailer’s message is ‘fashion with a small f’ as it picks up on trends and brings styles for everyone to debut runway show. Joan Collins declared the coats “very chic”, and has her eye on a graceful ivory evening dress with caped shoulders.
body: The show, held at the Design Museum for 310 guests including Ian Wright and Jamie Carragher, was a gamble on both sides. Would snobby fashionistas be traumatised by elasticated waistbands and practical rainwear? Would M&S customers be alienated by a world of £2,000 handbags and shoes you can’t walk in?

The style message was “fashion with a small f, not a capital F”, said the M&S womenswear director, Maddy Evans. The look was new enough to be compelling (sharp kilts instead of flouncy tiered skirts, low-rise slouchy denim replacing mom jeans), but pitched at a before-the-watershed comfort level. A judicious amount of catwalk theatre was added with some sauce (a very short skirt, the odd semi-visible nipple) and a little zeitgeisty styling (faux fur stoles, Charli xcx-adjacent sunglasses).

The real stunner is the price. All the clothes in this collection went on sale as the show began on Friday, with half of the pieces under £50. The most expensive, a leather coat, will retail for £450. The message – that catwalk style is for everyone – is a win for London fashion week, which has struggled to feel relevant to real lives as designer prices have soared during a cost of living crisis.

highlights.summary: You can skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, but while it's not necessarily the best choice, it's not a terrible one either. Whether it's the right one for you depends on where you're at in the game and what you're hoping to get from this part of it.
body: Below, we explain whether you should skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

If this is your first time playing through Fortune's Weave, then no, you absolutely should not skip the War Arc at the obelisk. It's an essential bridge connecting the end of the Flame Lords' first acts to Act 3. It's important even if you aren't interested in the story, too, since it gets you ready to face the much steeper challenges Act 3 throws at you. The battles become bigger and more demanding from here on out.

After that, it depends on what you're doing. The maps and story in Act 2 are the same for every character, except for a unique scene at the start and very end. You aren't missing anything there if you skip.

highlights.title: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)
highlights.summary: Three savory fillings, one simple technique, and no special equipment required.
body: Stuffed with savory fillings and wrapped in crisp nori, Japanese rice balls called onigiri are made for eating on the go. A convenience-store staple in Japan, they’re just as handy tucked into a lunch box or picnic basket.

The key to onigiri that hold their shape is properly cooked Japanese short-grain rice. Rinsing and soaking the rice helps it cook evenly; shaping it while still slightly warm helps the grains stick together. Use damp, salted hands to prevent sticking—no rice cooker or onigiri mold required.

This version offers three fillings: creamy tuna mayo, tart and salty umeboshi (pickled plums), or spicy kimchi. Once you’ve got the technique down, feel free to experiment with cooked salmon, spicy tuna, cod roe, leftover chicken salad, or crab meat. Just avoid anything too wet, which can make the rice balls difficult to shape.

Japanese short-grain rice, often labeled sushi rice at US supermarkets, is the best choice. When cooked, the grains cling together enough for the onigiri to hold their shape. Long-grain rice, such as jasmine or basmati, won’t hold together as well.
